title: E20 ROLLOUT BASED ON SCIENTIFIC VALIDATION AND EXTENSIVE STAKEHOLDER CONSULTATION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas E20 ROLLOUT BASED ON SCIENTIFIC VALIDATION AND EXTENSIVE STAKEHOLDER CONSULTATION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 3:04PM by PIB Delhi The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile manufacturers, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) and other technical institutions. The rollout of higher ethanol blends was undertaken only after extensive consultation with automobile manufacturers, SIAM, ARAI, component manufacturers, testing agencies and Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs). Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile manufacturers covering parameters such as engine durability, drivability, startability, corrosion resistance, material compatibility, emissions and fuel efficiency have confirmed that E20 is safe for use under prescribed standards. These studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. These extensive laboratory studies, field validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel. The Government's assessment is based not only on laboratory research but also on large-scale experience after nationwide implementation. India witnesses approximately 8 crore vehicles visiting retail outlets every day (around 80% petrol vehicles). This is evident from the fact that E15+ blended petrol has been in widespread use for over three-and-a-half years and E19-E20 fuel for over two-and-a-half years. More than 20 crore two-wheelers and over 3 crore petrol cars have been operating on these blends without any verified evidence of widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending. Manufacturer service data confirm that there is no abnormal corrosion, wear or reduction in vehicle life due to E20 fuel. Manufacturers continue to honour warranty obligations for vehicles using E20 fuel, providing further confidence in its safety and reliability. A leading OEM serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025-26, including approximately 1.5 crore vehicles that were not originally certified as E20-compatible, and reported no E20-linked corrosion, abnormal wear or reduction in component life. A leading 2-wheeler company has reported similar field experience. One OEM recently stated that data from 1.4 crore E20-operated vehicles tracked over an extended period showed no evidence of ethanol-induced corrosion. ARAI reaffirmed that vehicles undergo rigorous international-standard validation before reaching consumers. Automobile manufacturers, component suppliers, SIAM, ARAI, testing agencies and Oil Marketing Companies were associated with every stage of the scientific evaluation and phased rollout of E20. E20 was introduced only after successful validation of fuel systems, engine durability, drivability, material compatibility and emissions performance. These studies did not reveal any significant adverse impact on performance, durability or material compatibility in legacy vehicles under the prescribed operating conditions. Had automobile manufacturers not been fully satisfied with the results, they would neither have validated E20 fuel for older vehicles nor honoured warranty obligations . According to SIAM and ARAI, E20 improves acceleration and ride quality while reducing carbon emissions. Ethanol's higher-octane number supports modern high-compression engines and its higher heat of vaporisation improves combustion efficiency. This information was given by the MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS SHRI SURESH GOPI, in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. ***** TM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291661) आगंतुक पटल  : 314 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas E20 ROLLOUT BASED ON SCIENTIFIC VALIDATION AND EXTENSIVE STAKEHOLDER CONSULTATION प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: ASSESSMENT OF NATIONAL POWER GRID
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Power ASSESSMENT OF NATIONAL POWER GRID प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 2:53PM by PIB Delhi To strengthen the transmission infrastructure in line with the growing electricity demand, the Government of India notified the National Electricity Plan (Volume-II: Transmission) in 2024. The plan outlines the transmission system requirements for the period 2023–2032, commensurate with the projected generation capacity additions and anticipated growth in electricity demand across various emerging and conventional sectors of the economy (including electric mobility, data centres and industrial expansion across the country). The transmission planning also takes into account evolving load centres and new categories of electricity demand, while ensuring reliable integration of renewable energy. The transmission plan includes the addition of central and state transmission systems to meet the projected peak electricity demand of 388 GW by 2032. As per the plan, the transmission network is likely to expand from 5.09 lakh ckm (as on June, 2026) to 6.48 lakh ckm by 2032 and transformation capacity from 1,478 GVA (as on June, 2026) to 2,345 GVA. Also, the inter-regional transmission capacity is planned to increase from 120 GW (as on June, 2026) to 168 GW by the year 2032. The details of transmission capacity augmentation, grid modernization, deployment of smart grid technologies, battery energy storage systems and cyber security measures initiated during the last three years are as follows: Details of Transmission capacity augmentation: A total of 35,172 circuit km of transmission lines and 270,174 MVA of transformation capacity (220 kV and above) have been added during the last three years (FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26). Summary of the transmission lines and transformation capacity augmented is given at Table-I. Grid Modernization and deployment of smart grid technologies: Advanced grid support technologies such as Static Synchronous Compensators (STATCOMs), Synchronous Condensers (SynCONs), and other Flexible AC Transmission System (FACTS) devices are being deployed to enhance voltage stability, improve system strength, and support reliable integration of renewable energy. Further, several measures have been taken  to facilitate renewable energy integration, including establishment of Regional Energy Management Centres (REMCs) for renewable forecasting and real-time grid management, implementation of Automatic Generation Control (AGC) and Ancillary Services (SRAS/TRAS) for frequency regulation and balancing etc. Battery energy storage system (BESS): As on 30.06.2026, the installed capacity of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with capacity greater than 1 MWh is 2,927.85 MW / 8,660.20 MWh in the country. State wise details are given at Table-II. Cyber security measures: To strengthen the cyber security of Indian electricity grid, the Government of India has established a sector specific cyber security incident response team, namely, Computer Security Incident Response Team – Power (CSIRT-Power) in April, 2023 for coordinating, reporting, and responding to cyber security incidents in power sector. Cyber security measures undertaken during the last three years include approval of funding under Power System Development Fund (PSDF) for establishment of a Security Operations Centre (SOC) and a Network Operations Centre (NOC) to strengthen cyber security monitoring and incident response. Further, cyber security training programmes, workshops and capacity-building initiatives are being organized regularly in collaboration with the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), the National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC) and other institutions to enhance cyber security awareness and capabilities across the power sector. The Government has already initiated several measures to enhance the resilience, reliability and security of the national grid. In this regard, Task Force on Cyclone Resilient Robust Electricity Transmission and Distribution Infrastructure in Coastal Areas has recommended a comprehensive set of measures including, enhanced transmission planning based on higher contingency criteria, Critical Infrastructure Protection Framework, Mapping of Transmission and Distribution (T&D) infrastructure in cyclone affected zones, Designing of Distribution network in Ring or Mesh configuration, emergency restoration systems, Mobile substations, Mobile DGs set, digitalisation of power system assets, deployment of distributed energy resources, Standardization and use of Energy efficient equipment, use of advanced technologies such as Unmanned Arial Vehicles (UAVs) / Drones for inspection and monitoring, Underground transmission corridor along coastal highway project etc. Cyber resilience of the National Grid is being strengthened through round-the-clock(RTC) monitoring through the Security Operations Centre (SOC) and Network Operations Centre (NOC) at CSIRT-Power and GRID-INDIA; the system has also continuously been monitored by CERT-IN and National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC). Periodic Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VA/PT) of Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) infrastructure, and continuous capacity building in collaboration with reputed technical and national security institutions, so that preparedness keeps pace with the evolving cyber threat landscape. title: ASSESSMENTS ON ADEQUACY OF TRANSMISSION AND DISTRIBUTION INFRASTRUCTURE
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Power ASSESSMENTS ON ADEQUACY OF TRANSMISSION AND DISTRIBUTION INFRASTRUCTURE प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 2:44PM by PIB Delhi As per Section 7 of Electricity Act, 2003, setting up of a power plant is a de-licensed activity in the country. Any generating company may establish, operate and maintain a generating station without requiring a license under Electricity Act, 2003 if it complies with the technical standards relating to connectivity with the grid. Details of source-wise power generation capacity addition during FY 2026-27 (till June, 2026) is given at Table . Further, capacity addition is essential to meet the increasing electricity demand, particularly during peak load conditions, which ensures adequate generation availability, minimises the risk of power shortages and outages, and enhances the reliability. Details of assessments made by Central Electricity Authority (CEA) / Ministry of Power (MoP) on the adequacy of transmission and distribution infrastructure to absorb the added capacity are as follows: (i). Transmission Infrastructure: To strengthen the transmission infrastructure in line with the growing electricity demand, the Government of India notified the National Electricity Plan (Transmission), 2024, which outlines the transmission system requirements for the period 2023–2032. As per the plan, the transmission network is likely to expand from 5.09 lakh ckm (as on June, 2026) to 6.48 lakh ckm by 2032 and transformation capacity from 1,478 GVA (as on June, 2026) to 2,345 GVA. Also, the inter-regional transmission capacity is planned to increase from 120 GW as on June, 2026 to 168 GW by the year 2032. (ii). Distribution Infrastructure: Electricity being a concurrent subject, the supply and distribution of electricity is responsibility of the respective State Government/Distribution Utility. Hence, it is the responsibility of respective distribution utilities to take necessary measures to maintain an adequate and efficient distribution system in its area of operation. As per the perspective plan prepared by CEA based on expected demand, the sub-station capacity at 66/33/22 kV level is planned to be augmented from 605GVA (as on March 2026) to 711 GVA by 2030 and 872 GVA by 2035, Distribution Transformer capacity from 895 GVA to 1135 GVA by 2030 and 1631 GVA by 2035, 11 kV feeder length from 55.35 lakh ckm to 61.60 lakh ckm by 2030 and 70.77 lakh ckm by 2035, and LT lines from 84.75 lakh ckm to 95.69 lakh ckm by 2030 and 111.67 lakh ckm by 2035. Presently under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), launched by Government of India in July 2021 with the objective of making distribution utilities operationally efficient and financially viable, financial assistance is being provided to distribution utilities for upgradation of distribution infrastructure & smart metering works, Under the scheme, projects worth Rs. 1.53 lakh crore for loss reduction infrastructure and Rs. 1.31 lakh crore for smart metering works have been sanctioned across the country. The Government has put in place several measures and monitoring mechanisms to ensure the timely completion/ commissioning of transmission projects, Hydro Electric Projects (HEPs) and Thermal Power Projects which subsequently help in minimizing their time and cost overruns. The details are as under: Monitoring of Transmission Projects: To ensure timely commissioning of transmission projects, their implementation is closely monitored, and necessary interventions are undertaken to resolve challenges faced by developers. Transmission projects are monitored through periodic reviews by Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. (CTUIL), Central Electricity Authority (CEA) and by Ministry of Power. In addition, a review of projects is done through a dedicated platform viz. the Project Monitoring Group (PMG) under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade of India (DPIIT) and at the highest level of the Government through Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation (PRAGATI) portal. These mechanisms facilitate timely resolution of issues related to right of way, forest clearances, land acquisition, inter-agency coordination and other implementation challenges. (ii) Monitoring of Hydro Electric Projects (HEPs): Ministry of Power has issued guidelines to minimise time and cost overruns, established dispute avoidance and dispute resolution mechanisms for contractual issues. Additionally, an IT portal, Jal VidyutAmrit, has been developed for monitoring the progress of under-construction hydroelectric projects. Further, regular site visits are under taken by CEA to review project progress and resolve implementation bottlenecks. (iii) Monitoring of Thermal Power Projects: Ministry of Power regularly reviews the progress of under-construction projects to identify constraints and expedite the resolution of inter-ministerial and other outstanding issues. The Portal for Online Monitoring of Projects Thermal (PROPMT Portal), launched on 20.08.2024, is used to monitor project progress. Project-related issues are also taken up with the concerned State Governments and District Administrations, as required, and are reviewed on the PRAGATI portal to ensure proactive governance and timely implementation. (e) The efforts already made towards enhancing generation capacity utilisation, transmission and distribution efficiency and grid resilience have yielded encouraging results on electricity access, tariffs, energy security and economic growth: With the concerted efforts of Central and State Government, the average hours of supply in rural areas have increased from 12.5 hours in FY 14 to 22.6 hours in FY 26 and in urban areas the same has increased from 22.1 hours in FY 14 to 23.4 hours in FY 26. The Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) loss of distribution utilities at national level have reduced from 22.62 % in FY14 to 15.04 % in FY25. The gap between the Average Cost of Supply (ACS ) and the Average Revenue Realised (ARR), a key indicator of whether utilities are recovering their costs, narrowed sharply from ₹0.78 per unit in FY 14 to ₹0.06 per unit in FY25. A defining milestone was achieved on 29 July 2025, when India recorded its highest-ever renewable energy share in electricity generation. On that day, renewable sources met 51.5 per cent of the country’s total electricity demand of 203 GW. A record generation capacity addition of 64,695 MW was achieved during 2025-26. Out of this, 50,905 MW came from renewable energy sources (excluding large hydro) which represents the highest ever capacity addition in a single year, surpassing the previous record of 34,054 MW achieved in FY 2024–25. The energy shortage declined sharply to 0.0% in FY 2025-26, compared to 4.2% in FY 2013–14, reflecting a significant improvement in supply adequacy. India has achieved its commitment made at COP-26 by achieving the NDC goal of 50% of its installed electric power capacity from non-fossil fuel sources in 2025 i.e. five years ahead of the committed timeline of 2030. title: Understanding NAKSHA: Why Margao’s New Urban Mapping Pilot Protects Property Owners
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development Understanding NAKSHA: Why Margao’s New Urban Mapping Pilot Protects Property Owners प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 2:23PM by PIB Delhi As the Directorate of Settlement and Land Records (DSLR) prepares to launch its month-long inquiry under the NAKSHA pilot program in Margao and Cuncolim and Panaji city local conversations have been filled with an mix of curiosity and anxiety. Much of this apprehension stems from circulating rumors regarding the safety of land titles, potential boundary changes, and the rights of non-resident Goans. To ensure citizens can navigate this transition with confidence, it is essential to separate groundless anxiety from verifiable facts. NAKSHA, which stands for the National Geospatial Knowledge-based Land Survey of Urban Habitations, is a modern, GIS-based urban land parcel mapping initiative. Launched by the Department of Land Resources (DoLR) Government of India, the program operates under the broader framework of the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP). Unlike historical rural surveys, NAKSHA specifically leverages cutting-edge technology to create highly accurate digital maps for complex urban and peri-urban habitations across multiple states and Union Territories, ensuring our cities are future-ready. The most prominent concern among local property owners is whether this new digital survey will alter existing land records or titles. The state administration has addressed this directly with explicit assurances. Similarly, anxieties surrounding absentee landowners and Non-Resident Goans are entirely unfounded. Being away from the village or residing abroad during a field survey does not put a citizen's property at risk, nor does it cause them to lose their legal rights. The NAKSHA workflow features a highly structured process with multiple verification stages, including formally notified public verification windows, specifically designed to protect the interests of absent owners. Furthermore, legal ownership cannot be claimed by a neighbour simply because they happened to be physically present during a survey session. Property ownership continues to strictly follow legal processes and existing valid titles. It is also vital for the public to recognize that NAKSHA is neither a land acquisition scheme nor a tax collection drive. The project does not take over private land, nor is it being conducted to increase local property taxes. Its sole objective is to prepare reliable digital land maps that support superior town planning, infrastructure management, and efficient public utility layouts. Existing legal and title disputes will also remain unaffected, continuing to be resolved through the appropriate legal and administrative channels. Following the successful completion of the ground-truthing phase—where electronic mapping data is verified against actual field conditions—the formal inquiry process is set to run from 16 July 2026 to 14 August 2026. Property owners are directed to appear before the concerned Inspector at the Office of the Inspector of Survey and Land Records (ISLR), Osia Commercial Arcade, SGPDA Market, Margao, carrying their property title documents. Citizens do not need technical survey expertise to participate, as appointed officials will guide them step-by-step through the verification process. Embracing this modernisation drive ensures that your physical property matches your digital record, bringing long-term clarity and security to the entire community. ****** RC/HR (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291638) आगंतुक पटल  : 137 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati , Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Rural Development Understanding NAKSHA: Why Margao’s New Urban Mapping Pilot Protects Property Owners प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: TDB-DST supports M/s Sonic Biochem Extractions Pvt. Ltd., Indore, for Commercialization of Indigenous Functional and Textured Soya Protein Concentrates
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Science & Technology TDB-DST supports M/s Sonic Biochem Extractions Pvt. Ltd., Indore, for Commercialization of Indigenous Functional and Textured Soya Protein Concentrates प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 10:57AM by PIB Delhi Reinforcing India's commitment to self-reliance in value-added food processing and plant-based nutrition, the Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has extended financial assistance to M/s Sonic Biochem Extractions Pvt. Ltd., Indore (Madhya Pradesh) for the project titled “Development & Commercialization of Functional and Textured Soya Protein Concentrate(s).” The project aims to establish a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility for the commercial production of Functional Soya Protein Concentrate (FSPC) and Textured Soya Protein Concentrate (TSPC) using indigenous technology developed by the company. The initiative addresses the growing global demand for high-quality, non-GMO plant-based protein ingredients driven by increasing consumer preference for healthy, sustainable, and clean-label food products. It also aligns with the Government of India's vision of strengthening domestic food processing capabilities, promoting value addition in agriculture, and advancing Aatmanirbhar Bharat through import substitution and export-oriented manufacturing. With over two decades of experience in manufacturing and exporting non-GMO soya food ingredients, Sonic Biochem has developed an indigenous process for producing both FSPC and TSPC using Soya Protein Concentrate (SPC) as the primary raw material. Unlike conventional manufacturing processes that depend on comparatively expensive Soya Protein Isolate (SPI)—largely imported from countries such as China and the United States—the company's technology utilizes SPC indigenously developed and manufactured in-house while delivering comparable functional properties. This innovation significantly reduces production costs, enhances competitiveness, and strengthens India's self-reliance in the plant protein sector. The project will establish commercial-scale manufacturing capacity for these advanced protein ingredients, which find extensive applications across processed foods, plant-based meat alternatives, nutritional supplements, and functional food products. The technology is expected to reduce import dependence, generate new export opportunities, and strengthen India's position in the rapidly expanding global market for value-added plant proteins. By leveraging indigenous technology and locally sourced non-GMO soybeans, the project will create a robust domestic value chain for high-value protein ingredients while providing Indian food manufacturers with affordable access to globally competitive raw materials. The initiative is also expected to contribute to higher value realization for the agricultural sector and support the country's transition towards sustainable food systems. Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, stated, "Development of indigenous manufacturing capabilities for advanced plant protein ingredients is strategically important for strengthening India's food processing sector and expanding our presence in global markets. TDB remains committed to supporting technologies that promote value addition, reduce import dependence, and create globally competitive products under the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. This initiative is expected to generate significant foreign exchange savings while creating new export opportunities for India." Expressing gratitude for the support, the leadership of M/s Sonic Biochem Extractions Pvt. Ltd. stated that the assistance from TDB will enable the company to commercialize its indigenously developed technology at scale, strengthen India's leadership in non-GMO soya protein ingredients, and cater to the growing domestic and international demand for sustainable, high-quality plant-based nutrition solutions. ******** NKR/FT (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291532) आगंतुक पटल  : 292 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Science & Technology TDB-DST supports M/s Sonic Biochem Extractions Pvt. The initiative is also expected to contribute to higher value realization for the agricultural sector and support the country's transition towards sustainable food systems. TDB remains committed to supporting technologies that promote value addition, reduce import dependence, and create globally competitive products under the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. This initiative is expected to generate significant foreign exchange savings while creating new export opportunities for India." Expressing gratitude for the support, the leadership of M/s Sonic Biochem Extractions Pvt. Ltd. stated that the assistance from TDB will enable the company to commercialize its indigenously developed technology at scale, strengthen India's leadership in non-GMO soya protein ingredients, and cater to the growing domestic and international demand for sustainable, high-quality plant-based nutrition solutions. ******** NKR/FT (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291532)

title: Financial discipline and operational foresight drive SAIL’s Q1 FY27 profit surge
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Steel Financial discipline and operational foresight drive SAIL’s Q1 FY27 profit surge प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 1:42PM by PIB Delhi SAIL’s Q1 FY27 performance is not just about a sharp rise in profits y-o-y, it is about how financial acumen and operational foresight came together to deliver results. Commenting on SAIL’s performance in the first quarter of the FY27, Chairman & Managing Director, Dr. Ashok Kumar Panda said, “T his performance reflects the strength of SAIL’s integrated strategy. Even as the global headwinds generated due to volatility in the Middle East posed challenges, we demonstrated resilience through financial prudence combined with proactive operational measures. The performance during the quarter reflected a conscious drive towards efficiency improvement. Equally important was the company’s disciplined approach to cash flow management, strict financial controls and sharper working capital practices.” Going into the details on the prudent financial management strategy adopted by SAIL, he added that, “During the first quarter, the company contained borrowings and reduced the cost of borrowings through long standing financial credibility and further improvement in management of cash flows and debt. Liquidity remained strong, and both the debt–equity ratio and net debt–EBITDA profile showed marked improvement, highlighting SAIL’s success in reducing debt exposure while sustaining profitability.” Q1 FY27 reflected progress in company’s product mix and investment priorities. The proportion of finished steel in the total saleable steel improved to 89% in Q1 FY27 from 86% over CPLY, indicating a gradual reduction of semis in the company’s overall product basket. The percentage of value‑added steel dispatches also increased by 7.5% in Q1 FY27 over CPLY, reinforcing SAIL’s focus on quality‑driven growth. At the same time, CAPEX exceeded the target from ₹2,306 Crore to ₹2,575 Crore, highlighting the company’s strong commitment to strategic investments and proactive allocation of resources towards capacity expansion and modernization. The quarter also showcased SAIL’s ability to translate strategy into operational resilience. Blast furnace productivity improved, steelmaking economics were reinforced through optimized ferro‑alloys and flux consumption, and scheduled capital repairs were advanced proactively to secure stability for the coming quarters . Dr. Panda further elaborated that “Our focus on operational foresight ensured uninterrupted performance despite supply chain disruptions. While limestone requirements were met through a balanced mix of indigenous and external sources, alternate arrangements for Propane gas safeguarded continuity.” The focused thrust on mining operations delivered significant results by unlocking the full potential of SAIL's captive mines. Enhanced iron ore production enabled the Company to fully meet its internal raw material requirements while marketing surplus ore in the domestic market. As a result, iron ore sales during Q1FY27 registered an impressive 269% growth over the corresponding period of the previous year. This exceptional performance provided a significant boost to the Company's bottom line and underscored the strategic strength of SAIL's integrated business model, wherein value creation across the mining and steel value chain directly translates into superior operational and financial performance. Taken together, these developments underscore how SAIL is not only delivering financial resilience but also reshaping its product portfolio and investing in future‑ready infrastructure - laying the foundation for sustained competitiveness in a volatile global environment. **** AG (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291614) आगंतुक पटल  : 90 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Bengali Ministry of Steel Financial discipline and operational foresight drive SAIL’s Q1 FY27 profit surge प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: MOIL Reports Strong Performance in Q1 FY 2026-27; Profit After Tax Up by 70%
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Steel MOIL Reports Strong Performance in Q1 FY 2026-27; Profit After Tax Up by 70% प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 1:41PM by PIB Delhi The Board of Directors of MOIL Limited approved the financial and operational results for the first quarter of FY 2026-27 (Q1 FY27). The company recorded steady growth across production, sales volume, and overall profitability. Financial Highlights (Q1 FY 2026-27 vs Q1 FY 2025-26): Revenue from Operations: Increased by 7% to ₹370.88 crore, up from ₹348.06 crore. Total Revenue: Rose by 6% to ₹391.13 crore compared to ₹370.52 crore. Profit Before Tax (PBT): Registered a 75% increase to ₹111.62 crore from ₹63.82 crore. Profit After Tax (PAT): Increased by 70% to ₹87.62 crore compared to ₹51.51 crore. Net Sales Realization (NSR): Reached ₹9,749 per MT, reflecting a 10% gain over ₹8,884 per MT in the corresponding previous quarter. Operational Highlights: Manganese Ore Production: Stood at 507,605 MT, marking a 1% increase over 502,260 MT recorded in Q1 FY26. Manganese Ore Sales: Reached 369,049 MT, up by 4% from 356,196 MT in the same period last year. Appreciating the efforts of the team, MOIL management said, "These results reflect the dedication and hard work of our entire workforce. The operational discipline and commitment shown by our team have enabled the company to maintain growth across key metrics. As we move forward, MOIL remains focused on achieving higher production targets, improving operational efficiency, and meeting the growing requirements of the domestic steel industry." MOIL Limited is a Schedule ‘A’ Miniratna Category-I Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Steel, Government of India. It is the largest producer of manganese ore in the country, operating underground and open-cast mines across Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. ***** AG (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291611) आगंतुक पटल  : 90 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Steel MOIL Reports Strong Performance in Q1 FY 2026-27; Profit After Tax Up by 70% प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Union Minister Shri Giriraj Singh to Inaugurate Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology at IIT Delhi on 3 August
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles Union Minister Shri Giriraj Singh to Inaugurate Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology at IIT Delhi on 3 August Centre of Excellence to Strengthen India's Handloom Sector through Research, Innovation and Digital Technologies and to boost Competitiveness, Sustainability and Global Outreach of India's Handloom Sector प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 3:36PM by PIB Delhi In a major step towards building a technology-driven, future-ready handloom ecosystem, the Union Minister of Textiles Shri Giriraj Singh will inaugurate the Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology (CoE-HT) at IIT Delhi on 3 August 2026. Union Minister of State for Textiles Shri Pabitra Margherita, Secretary Textiles, Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Dr. M. Beena will also grace the inauguration ceremony along with senior officials from Ministry of Textiles and IIT Delhi. The Centre of Excellence established with a Government of India investment of ₹11.99 crore, aims to integrate India's rich handloom heritage with cutting-edge research, innovation and digital technologies to strengthen the sector's competitiveness, sustainability and global outreach. This centre will serve as a national knowledge and innovation hub, bringing together academia, industry, designers, technologists, startups and handloom institutions to develop advanced solutions for the handloom sector. Its focus areas include loom modernization and ergonomics, artificial intelligence, sustainability, functional innovation, digital knowledge systems and entrepreneurship. Over the next five years, the Centre will develop a national digital repository of handloom knowledge, create AI-enabled tools, develop improved loom technologies, facilitate patents and research, incubate startups, and train weavers, faculty members and handloom professionals across the country. The launch of the Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology marks a significant milestone in the Government's efforts to modernize the handloom sector while preserving India's rich weaving traditions. By fostering research, innovation and entrepreneurship, the Centre is expected to create a robust ecosystem that empowers weavers, enhances productivity, promotes sustainable practices and positions Indian handloom for emerging domestic and global opportunities. India's handloom sector supports more than 35 lakh weavers and allied workers, with women constituting nearly 70 per cent of the workforce. While preserving centuries-old weaving traditions, the sector also faces challenges relating to productivity, technology adoption, traceability, authenticity, sustainability and market competitiveness. The Centre has been conceived to address these challenges through research, innovation, capacity building and technology transfer. The inaugural programme will also witness the launch of five flagship initiatives that showcase the Centre's vision of combining tradition with technology: Handloom 4.0 – a digital companion for every loom, enabling weavers to assess productivity & sustainability, helping cooperatives and government agencies to deliver timely last-mile assistance. Handloom e-Vidya , a problem‑linked digital learning and knowledge hub that provides practical, curated solutions for weavers, students and other key stakeholders in the handloom ecosystem. HandloomX , an accelerator and incubation platform to nurture startups and innovations across the handloom value chain. Kalagriha Handloom Studio (GenZ Design Studio), aimed at connecting handloom with next-generation consumers through digital visualization, customization and product authentication. Threads of Valour , an initiative promoting circularity by transforming recycled defence textiles into premium handloom products. ******** MAM/VN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291701) आगंतुक पटल  : 79 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati Ministry of Textiles Union Minister Shri Giriraj Singh to Inaugurate Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology at IIT Delhi on 3 August Centre of Excellence to Strengthen India's Handloom Sector through Research, Innovation and Digital Technologies and to boost Competitiveness, Sustainability and Global Outreach of India's Handloom Sector प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGES ON CHANGPA TRIBAL COMMUNITY IN LADAKH
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGES ON CHANGPA TRIBAL COMMUNITY IN LADAKH प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 1:48PM by PIB Delhi Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs has not undertaken any study to assess the impact of climate change, shrinking grazing pastures, changing snowfall patterns and declining livestock productivity on the livelihood and traditional nomadic lifestyle of the Changpa tribal community in Ladakh. Changpa families, being members of a Scheduled Tribe, are eligible beneficiaries under the welfare and livelihood schemes implemented by this Ministry and other line Ministries/Departments during the last five years, including: (i) Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN); (ii) Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA); (iii) Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS); (iv) Pre-Matric, Post-Matric and National Overseas Scholarships for Scheduled Tribe students; (v) Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM); Yes. Under the umbrella of DAJGUA, targeted interventions have been taken up for remote tribal habitations including Mobile Medical Units; mobile network delivery; residential hostel facilities; pucca housing under PM-AWAS (Gramin) etc. Additionally, livelihood and income-enhancement support for Pashmina wool production, marketing linkages and value addition is being undertaken through TRIFED. Under PMJVM scheme, TRIFED has released an amount of ₹15 lakhs for establishment of the VDVK, Durbuk. The details of funds sanctioned and released for EMRSs to the UT of Ladakh in last 5 years is as follows: Financial Year Rs. in lakhs 2021-22 10.00 2022-23 450.00 2023-24 800.00 2024-25 17.41 2025-26 400.00 To strengthen long-term socio-economic resilience and preserve the traditional culture and livelihood of the Changpa community, the following measures, among others, are being taken: Saturation of basic infrastructure and services in Changthang habitations under PM-JANMAN/DAJGUA; During the last five years, TRIFED has procured Pashmina products (Shawls and Stoles) worth ₹18,847,291 from Ladakh-based artisans. Since the raw Pashmina used in these products is sourced from the Changpa community, these procurements have indirectly contributed to the livelihood and economic well-being of the Changpa pastoralists. Further, an empanelment camp is proposed to be organised in the Changthang region in August’2026 with the objective of identifying and empanelling eligible artisans from the Changpa Tribal Community. This initiative is expected to facilitate their direct participation in marketing and procurement programmes, thereby strengthening their livelihood opportunities. Documentation and promotion of Changpa culture, language and traditional knowledge through tribal research institute. *** RN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291621) आगंतुक पटल  : 106 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Tribal Affairs IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGES ON CHANGPA TRIBAL COMMUNITY IN LADAKH प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: BENEFITS FOR STs IN UNION TERRITORRIES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs BENEFITS FOR STs IN UNION TERRITORRIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 1:45PM by PIB Delhi Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that Union Territory-wise Scheduled Tribe (ST) population as per Census,2011: S. No. UT ST Population(in no.’s) 1 Jammu & Kashmir 12,75,106 2 Ladhak 2,18,193 3 Andaman & Nicobar Islands 28,530 4 Chandigarh NST 5 Dadra & Nagar haveli and Daman Diu 1,93,927 6 Lakshadweep 61,120 7 Puducherry NST 8 Delhi NST Note:’NST’ means No Notified Scheduled Tribes The latest census-based figures of ST population will be available after the release of the next population census. The Government continues to support the welfare and socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes through various schemes and interventions of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. These include Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) for saturation of infrastructure and basic services in tribal villages; Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) for the holistic development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs); Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) for providing quality residential education to tribal students; Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, National Scholarship for Higher Education, National Fellowship and National Overseas Scholarship Schemes for educational support; Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution for bridging critical infrastructure gaps in Scheduled Areas and tribal areas; Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organisations for education, health and livelihood initiatives; Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM), National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) and Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-ST) for promoting sustainable livelihoods, entrepreneurship and concessional credit; and Tribal Research, Information, Education, Communication and Events (TRI-ECE) for research, documentation and capacity building. In addition, health, education, drinking water, connectivity and other infrastructure-related interventions are being implemented through convergence with the concerned Ministries/Departments. As per available information no proposal for grant of Scheduled Tribe status to any community on the basis of duration of residence in the UT of Delhi is under consideration in this Ministry. Grant of Scheduled Tribe status is governed by Article 342 of the Constitution, under which a community can be specified as a Scheduled Tribe only through a notification issued by the President after consultation with the Governor/Administrator concerned, and any subsequent inclusion or exclusion is affected only by an Act of Parliament amending the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950. Such proposals are examined against the criteria recommended by the Lokur Committee (1965) — namely, indications of primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact with the community at large, and social and economic backwardness — and require a specific recommendation from the concerned State Government/UT Administration, followed by concurrence of the Registrar General of India and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes. Reservation for Scheduled Tribes in Union Territories is presently provided as under: (i) Political institutions: Reservation of seats for STs in the UT Legislative Assemblies/Panchayats/Municipalities is provided in proportion to their population under the respective Government of Union Territories Act, 1963, the Delimitation Act, 2002 and other applicable local laws, in Union Territories having notified ST population, namely Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. No such reservation applies in Chandigarh, Delhi and Puducherry, since no ST is notified therein. (ii) Administrative services: Reservation in direct recruitment to civil posts and services under the Union Territory administrations follows the reservation policy of the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT), Government of India, which prescribes 7.5% reservation for Scheduled Tribes at the all-India level. In Union Territories with a predominant or substantial ST population (such as Lakshadweep and Dadra & Nagar Haveli), a higher percentage of reservation is provided in local/UT cadre recruitment, commensurate with the local ST population, as notified by the respective UT Administration from time to time. title: STATUS OF EMRSs
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs STATUS OF EMRSs प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 1:44PM by PIB Delhi Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that as on date, 728 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) are approved across the country out of which 508 are functional. In Bihar, 03 EMRSs have been approved, of which 02 EMRSs are functional. The inauguration of 43 new EMRSs during 2025-26 is an effort to expand the EMRS network in the country. Various steps have been undertaken to enhance the quality of education and sports facilities in EMRSs across the country which are well-equipped classrooms with modern teaching aids, bridge courses, remedial classes science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, art, and sports, smart classrooms for digital education, computer labs with internet access, skill development and vocational training programs on a pparel, Automotive, AR/VR, AI, Beauty & Wellness, Agriculture, Electronics, and retail to enhance employability, etc. To address the issue of vacancies, 9111 teaching & non -teaching staff have already been recruited and examination has been conducted for another batch of 7267 teaching & non -teaching staff for EMRSs across the country. In addition, State Governments have also been advised to depute staff on deputation and contract basis to address the issue of vacancies so that academic activities are not hampered. In order to bridge the infrastructure gap in EMRSs, several measures have been taken such as Standardised designs ensuring modern academic facilities, hostels, staff quarters, and sports infrastructure; additional grants for upgradation of old schools; regular monitoring through third-party inspections etc. Further, National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) continuously follows up with the State Governments and the execution agencies to fast-track construction of EMRSs and to make them functional at the earliest. Besides, State Governments have also been advised to make the EMRS functional in alternative buildings, wherever feasible. The expansion of EMRSs aligns with the Government's objectives of inclusive education and empowerment of tribal communities in the following manner: EMRSs provide access to quality residential education to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students in remote and tribal-dominated areas, thereby reducing educational disparities. The scheme promotes equitable access to educational opportunities by providing free education along with boarding and lodging facilities. EMRSs focus on the holistic development of tribal students through academic excellence, sports, skill development, and extracurricular activities. The scheme enhances educational attainment, employability and leadership potential among tribal youth, contributing to their socio-economic empowerment. The expansion of EMRSs supports the Government's commitment to inclusive and accessible education for tribal communities across the country. In Bihar, 03 EMRSs have been approved, of which 02 EMRSs are functional. The inauguration of 43 new EMRSs during 2025-26 is an effort to expand the EMRS network in the country. Various steps have been undertaken to enhance the quality of education and sports facilities in EMRSs across the country which are well-equipped classrooms with modern teaching aids, bridge courses, remedial classes science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, art, and sports, smart classrooms for digital education, computer labs with internet access, skill development and vocational training programs on a pparel, Automotive, AR/VR, AI, Beauty & Wellness, Agriculture, Electronics, and retail to enhance employability, etc. To address the issue of vacancies, 9111 teaching & non -teaching staff have already been recruited and examination has been conducted for another batch of 7267 teaching & non -teaching staff for EMRSs across the country. In addition, State Governments have also been advised to depute staff on deputation and contract basis to address the issue of vacancies so that academic activities are not hampered. In order to bridge the infrastructure gap in EMRSs, several measures have been taken such as Standardised designs ensuring modern academic facilities, hostels, staff quarters, and sports infrastructure; additional grants for upgradation of old schools; regular monitoring through third-party inspections etc. Further, National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) continuously follows up with the State Governments and the execution agencies to fast-track construction of EMRSs and to make them functional at the earliest. Besides, State Governments have also been advised to make the EMRS functional in alternative buildings, wherever feasible. The expansion of EMRSs aligns with the Government's objectives of inclusive education and empowerment of tribal communities in the following manner: EMRSs provide access to quality residential education to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students in remote and tribal-dominated areas, thereby reducing educational disparities. The scheme promotes equitable access to educational opportunities by providing free education along with boarding and lodging facilities. EMRSs focus on the holistic development of tribal students through academic excellence, sports, skill development, and extracurricular activities. The scheme enhances educational attainment, employability and leadership potential among tribal youth, contributing to their socio-economic empowerment. The expansion of EMRSs supports the Government's commitment to inclusive and accessible education for tribal communities across the country. RN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291615)

title: Scheduled Tribes in Kerala
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs Scheduled Tribes in Kerala प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 1:40PM by PIB Delhi Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that as per Census 2011, the Scheduled Tribe (ST) population of Kerala is 4,84,839, constituting 1.45 per cent of the total population of the State. The districts having the highest Scheduled Tribe population are Wayanad, Idukki, Palakkad, Kasaragod and Kannur. The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 is implemented by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations, while the Ministry of Tribal Affairs monitors its implementation through Monthly Progress Reports received from them. As per MPR of MoTA, 2,923 Individual Forest Rights (IFR) titles and 110 Community Forest Rights (CFR) titles, aggregating 3033 forest rights titles, have been distributed under the Act. The Government accords high priority to the socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes, including those residing in Kerala. Issues relating to land rights, education, health, nutrition and livelihood are addressed through implementation of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and various schemes of the Central and State Governments. Matters relating to land alienation are dealt with by the State Government under the applicable State laws, while health and nutrition interventions are implemented through convergence under various Central and State Government programmes. The year wise details of funds released to the Government of Kerala under Tribal sub Plan and other centrally sponsored schemes: (Rs. In Crores) Sl .No. Scheme 2021-22 2022-23 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 1 Tribal Sub Plan Scheme # 781.36 859.50 859.50 859.50 920.00 2 Support to Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) - - - 3.00 1.04 3 Pre-Matric Scholarship for ST Students 3.47 - 4.36 1.00 0.75 4 Post-Matric Scholarship for ST Students 25.16 - 46.89 29.00 62.36 5 PM JANMAN * - - 2.29 * - - 6 Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution - 8.18 19.10 3.96 - 7 PMAAGY - - 0.61 0.30 - *: The PM JANMAN scheme was launched on 15 November 2023. #: State TSP The government continues to support the welfare and development of Scheduled tribes in Kerala through various interventions: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan: Hon'ble PM launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan Hon'ble PM launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) on 2nd October, 2024. The Abhiyan comprises of 25 interventions implemented by 17-line Ministries and aims to saturate infrastructural gaps in 63,843 villages, provide social infrastructure like hostels, Anganwadi facilities and mobile medical units and set up Van Dhan Vikas Kendras to provide livelihood opportunities benefiting more than 5 crore tribals in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks in 30 States/UTs in 5 years. The Abhiyan has a total budgetary outlay of Rs.79,156 Cr (Central share: ₹56,333 Cr and State share: ₹22,823 Cr) Pre-Matric Scholarships to ST students : The scheme is applicable to students who are studying in Classes IX –X. Parental income from all sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Scholarship of Rs.225/-per month for day scholars and Rs.525/-per month for hostellers is given for a period of 10 months in a year. Scholarship is disbursed through the State Government/UT Administration. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except North East and Hills States/UT like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10.For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share. Post Matric Scholarship to ST students: The objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the Scheduled Tribe students studying at post-matriculation or post-secondary levels to enable them to complete their education. Parental income from all sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Compulsory fees charged by educational institutions are reimbursed subject to the limit fixed by the concerned State Fee fixation committee and scholarship amount of Rs.230 to Rs.1200 per month, depending upon the course of study is paid. The Scheme is implemented by the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except NE and Hilly States/UT of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10. For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share. National Scholarship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students (earlier known as Top Class Scholarship Scheme): Under this Scheme, Scholarship is provided for pursuing Graduate/Post Graduate courses in the selected top-class Government and Non-Government Institutes in professional fields such as Management, Medicine, Engineering, Information Technology, Law etc. All the ST students, with annual parental income is not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs and studying in the 265 notified institutes by the Ministry, are eligible to receive scholarship. This scheme is started from year 2007-08 (b) National Fellowship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students: It is a Central Sector Scheme, fully funded by Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs to grant scholarship to meritorious ST students for pursuing Ph.D in India after completion of Master degree. This scheme is started from year 2005-06. The total number of fresh fellowships for Ph.D every year will be 750. ST students with a minimum of 55% marks in Master Degree up to the age of 36 years are eligible to apply for fellowship under the Scheme. The value of fellowship is at par with UGC rates. National Overseas Scholarship for ST students: It is a Central Sector Scheme of Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs under which scholarships are given to the meritorious Schedule Tribe (ST) students for pursuing higher education in top 1000 ranked (as per latest QS world ranking) Institutes/Universities abroad. This scheme is started from year 1954-55. The Scheme is implemented through the Indian Embassies/Missions abroad, Ministry of External Aﬀairs. Twenty awards are given every year. ST students with annual family income not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs are eligible to apply for the Scholarship under the Scheme. Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN): Government launched Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) for socio-economic development of 75 PVTG communities residing in 18 states and one UT. The mission aims to provide basic facilities such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities in 3 years. These objectives are planned to be met through 11 interventions including Hostels and Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) implemented by 9-line Ministries. PM JANMAN has total budgetary outlay of Rs.24,104 Cr (Central share: ₹15336 Cr and State share: ₹8768 Cr). Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution : Under the Proviso to Article 275(1) of Constitution, Grants are released to States, having ST population for raising the level of administration in Scheduled Areas and for the welfare of tribal people. This is a Special Area Programme and 100% grants are provided to States. Funds are released to the State Governments depending on the felt needs of ST population to bridge the gap in infrastructure activities in the fields of education, health, skill development, livelihood, drinking water, sanitation, etc. Grant-in Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes: Under the scheme of Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes, the Ministry funds projects in the fields of education and health, covering residential schools, non-residential schools, hostels, mobile dispensaries, ten or more bedded hospitals, livelihood, etc. Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS): The Scheme provides quality residential education to Scheduled Tribe students in remote and tribal areas with the objective of enabling them to access quality education comparable to the best institutions in the country. The schools provide modern educational infrastructure along with facilities for holistic development of tribal students. Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM): The Mission promotes sustainable livelihoods of Scheduled Tribes through value addition, entrepreneurship development, marketing support and strengthening of tribal producer organisations, with emphasis on value chains based on Minor Forest Produce and other tribal products. Tribal Research, Information, Education, Communication and Events (TRI-ECE): The Scheme supports Tribal Research Institutes for research, documentation, capacity building, preservation and promotion of tribal culture, awareness generation, information dissemination and evidence-based policy support. National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC): under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is an apex organisation set up exclusively for economic development of Scheduled Tribes implements various schemes for livelihood generation. NSTFDC extends concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled Tribe communities. Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-ST): The Scheme is implemented through the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) to provide concessional venture capital assistance to Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs for establishment and expansion of income-generating enterprises. Strengthening of health, education, drinking water, connectivity and other infrastructure through convergence with Ministries/Departments and the Government of Kerala. title: STRENGTHENING AND EXPANSION OF EMRSs
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs STRENGTHENING AND EXPANSION OF EMRSs प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 1:39PM by PIB Delhi Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the scheme of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) for providing quality education to tribal students in their own environment preserving local art and culture. EMRS are established in tribal dominated blocks having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as per Census 2011. As on date, 728 EMRSs have been approved out of which 508 are functional across the country. Various steps have been undertaken to enhance the quality of education and extra-curricular activities in EMRSs across the country viz. well-equipped classrooms with modern teaching aids, bridge courses, remedial classes science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, art, and sports, smart classrooms for digital education, computer labs with internet access, skill development and vocational training programs on a pparel, Automotive, AR/VR, AI, Beauty & Wellness, Agriculture, Electronics, and retail to enhance employability, etc. To strengthen digital learning in EMRSs, smart classrooms, digital boards, computer labs with internet connectivity, and a dedicated DTH TV have been provided. Eklavya channel provides curriculum-based learning and competitive exam content for Classes 9th to 12th, ensuring continuous access to quality educational resources. At present there are 284 Smart classrooms in EMRSs across the country including the blocks of Sohagpur, Jaitpur, Anuppur and Umaria located in Shahdol Lok Sabha Constituency. Further, National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) continuously follows up with the State Governments and the execution agencies to expedite construction of EMRSs and to make them functional at the earliest. Besides, State Governments have also been advised to make the EMRS functional in alternate buildings, wherever feasible. To strengthen the governance, management and operation of Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs), various institutional reforms have been taken such as; Establishment of National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) as an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to provide overall policy direction, academic support, monitoring, capacity building, recruitment, standardization of processes and implementation of the EMRS Scheme across the country; State EMRS Societies to oversee the implementation, administration and day-to-day management of EMRSs within their jurisdictions; District Level EMRS Committees , under the Chairmanship of the District Collector/District Magistrate s to strengthen local oversight and resolve local implementation issues. Comprehensive operational guidelines and circulars covering academic administration, financial management, procurement, student welfare, health and safety, hostel management, and grievance redressal to ensure uniform standards across all EMRSs. Centralized recruitment mechanism through the EMRS Staff Selection Examination (ESSE) has been instituted to ensure the appointment of qualified and competent teaching and non-teaching personnel across EMRSs. Structured induction programmes, regular in-service training, and continuous capacity-building initiatives to enhance professional competencies and strengthen institutional effectiveness. In order to provide timely funds to EMRSs, NESTS is releasing recurring grant directly to the schools. These institutional reforms have strengthened accountability, coordination, monitoring and thereby improving overall management of EMRSs.The State-wise details of sanctioned, operational and construction status of EMRSs, including Odisha, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh, are at Annexure I. The details of sanctioned, operational and construction status of EMRSs in Keonjhar and Shahdol Parliament Constituency are at Annexure II. None of the blocks in Araria Lok Sabha Constituency fulfill the prescribed criteria for establishing EMRS. To address the issue of vacancies, 9111 teaching & non -teaching staff have already been recruited and examination has been conducted for another batch of 7267 teaching & non -teaching staff for EMRSs across the country. Total 514 teaching staff have been posted in EMRSs across Odisha in first phase of recruitment including 59 teaching staff in EMRSs in Keonjhar Lok Sabha constituency. In addition, State Governments have also been advised to depute staff on deputation and contract basis to address the issue of vacancies so that academic activities are not hampered. EMRSs are well equipped with modern design with separate Boys’ and Girls’ Hostels, integrated dining and kitchen facilities, quarters for teaching and non-teaching staff, well-ventilated classrooms with modern teaching aids, science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, art and sports to preserve local art and culture. title: EVICTION OF TRIBAL COMMUNITIES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs EVICTION OF TRIBAL COMMUNITIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 1:38PM by PIB Delhi Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that the representations that were received in the Ministry from Van Gujjar communities of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh concerning the issues related to rights under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, (in short FRA), 2006, were examined. Since the implementation of the FRA lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations, these representations were forwarded to the respective State Governments and concerned District Administrations for examination and taking necessary action in accordance with the provisions of the FRA and other applicable laws. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has been exhorting all State Governments/UT Administration to abide by the provisions contained in FRA. Regular review meetings to assess the progress of FRA etc are held with State Governments/UT Administration. Further, grievances /representations received in the Ministry regarding violation of provisions of FRA are forwarded to the States/UTs concerned, to ensure that legitimate claimants are not denied their forest rights. Ministry of Tribal Affairs has advised States/UTs to undertake periodic training of Sub-Divisional Level Committee (SDLC) / District Level Committee (DLC) members and to ensure adherence to due process under the FRA. All training modules/ pamphlets are regularly shared with States/UTs. Capacity Building and training measures are being undertaken by State Governments/UT Administrations. *** RN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291608) आगंतुक पटल  : 60 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Tribal Affairs EVICTION OF TRIBAL COMMUNITIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: EXPANSION OF EMRS IN WEST BENGAL
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs EXPANSION OF EMRS IN WEST BENGAL प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 1:35PM by PIB Delhi Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that Bundwan block of Purulia district in West Bengal is the only block meeting the prescribed criteria for establishment of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS). The land for said block has been identified by State Government. As reported by the State Government, EMRS in Kalimpong is functional in alternate building and the construction of permanent building has commenced. A total of Rs 20.91 Cr has been approved for EMRS Kalimpong out of which Rs. 9.96 Cr has been released.                 30 JUL 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) was launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on 15th November, 2023 for the socio-economic development of the 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) communities residing in 18 States including Gujarat and one Union Territory. The mission aims to provide basic facilities to improve their socio-economic conditions such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities. These objectives are being met through 11 interventions implemented by 9-line Ministries. Based on the data captured, State/UT- wise, PVTG villages, habitations and population is tabulated at Annexure II . Affordable Nutrition for Every Indian: Jan Aushadhi Nutraceuticals
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder Affordable Nutrition for Every Indian:  Jan Aushadhi Nutraceuticals प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 11:05AM by PIB Delhi In an increasingly health-conscious India, nutraceuticals have gained recognition as an essential part of overall well-being. Be it for school-going children or senior citizens, dietary supplements, herbal products that include vitamins & minerals, herbs & botanicals, probiotics, etc., have found wide acceptance.  Yet, affordability continues to be a challenge for millions of families seeking nutritional supplements. The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) is addressing this gap with its nutraceutical basket. From nutrition bars to disease-specific formulations, the Jan Aushadhi nutraceuticals Basket is making nutrition supplements more accessible to people across India. Nutrition for Diverse Needs The Jan Aushadhi portfolio is designed to respond to the varied needs of young, old, women, and people with different health issues. The range includes protein supplements, immunity products, nutritional foods and specialised formulations for individuals with specific dietary requirements. Manufactured in accordance with prescribed quality standards and offered at affordable prices, these products aim to make regular nutritional support more accessible without placing an undue burden on household budgets . Convenient Nutrition for Active Lifestyles Nutrient-dense Jan Aushadhi Protein Bar & Jan Aushadhi Immunity Bar offer a portable source of nourishment for children, working professionals and fitness enthusiasts. Available in chocolate flavour in a 35-gram pack, protein bar provides a convenient way to supplement daily protein intake while on the go. Enriched with Immunity-Supporting Ingredients tasty Immunity Bar provides energy and strengthens body’s protective barriers. These nutrition bars offer an economical alternative for consumers craving a quick snack but averse to junk food. For a more substantial protein supplement, 100% Whey Protein Powder & Jan Aushadhi Protein Powder support daily protein intake and muscle recovery, making it suitable for fitness enthusiasts. Protein Powder is available in Vanilla and Kesar Pista flavours, giving consumers greater choice. Supporting Women's Nutritional Needs Women have distinct nutritional requirements at different stages of life.  Jan Aushadhi Women Protein Boost is formulated to support daily protein intake, energy levels, and healthy bones and muscles. Available in chocolate and vanilla flavours, the 250-gram pack is priced at ₹204.66. By offering specialised nutrition at affordable rates, this product seeks to make it easier for more women to incorporate nutritional supplementation into their daily routines. Nutrition Designed for Specific Health Needs For individuals managing specific health conditions such as Diabetes, Kidney problems etc, dietary requirements can be more complex. Diabetes Care Protein Powder from JanAushadhi complements the nutritional requirements of people living with diabetes. For individuals with kidney-related conditions, Renal Care Protein Powder is available in both Low Protein and High Protein variants, allowing the choice of formulation to be guided by medical advice and individual dietary needs. Jan Aushadhi Poshan: Everyday Nutrition for Families For affordable everyday nutritional support for everyone in the family, the Jan Aushadhi Poshan range offers malt-based nutritional food enriched with essential vitamins and minerals. Available in regular malt and cocoa variants, the range includes: Malt Based Food, 500 g: ₹160.17 Malt Based Food with Cocoa, 500 g: ₹164.62 Malt Based Food with Cocoa Sachet, 30 g: ₹8.90 The multiple pack sizes offer flexibility for different consumption needs and budgets. Easy to prepare and suitable for regular consumption, the Poshan range provides families with an accessible nutritional supplement for everyday use. Making Quality Nutrition More Accessible These products highlight the growing importance of nutrition as part of a broader approach to health management. While specialised nutritional products should be used in accordance with professional medical and dietary guidance, affordable access can help make appropriate nutritional support more attainable for families. For overall well-being, lifestyle choices that include quality nutrition cannot be stressed more.  Families are increasingly opting to make healthy choices when it comes to food and nutrition supplements. By offering affordable alternatives to expensive branded nutrition supplements through the Jan Aushadhi Kendra network, PMBJP is ensuring that quality nutritional support is not limited by income. Affordable medicines remain the core of PMBJP, but nutrition is an essential part of the same larger health journey. Whether it is a student seeking convenient nourishment, a working professional managing a demanding routine, a homemaker supporting family nutrition, a senior citizen with specific dietary needs or an individual managing a health condition, access to appropriate nutrition can play an important role in supporting well-being. By combining quality, affordability and accessibility, the Jan Aushadhi nutraceutical range is helping make nutrition a more attainable choice for Indian families reinforcing the vision of “Quality Healthcare and Nutrition for All.” Reference: Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers See in PDF *** PIB Research (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291539) आगंतुक पटल  : 668 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Manipuri , Gujarati , Tamil PIB Backgrounder Affordable Nutrition for Every Indian:  Jan Aushadhi Nutraceuticals प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                        30 JUL 2026 11:05AM by PIB Delhi In an increasingly health-conscious India, nutraceuticals have gained recognition as an essential part of overall well-being. Be it for school-going children or senior citizens, dietary supplements, herbal products that include vitamins & minerals, herbs & botanicals, probiotics, etc., have found wide acceptance.  Yet, affordability continues to be a challenge for millions of families seeking nutritional supplements. The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) is addressing this gap with its nutraceutical basket. From nutrition bars to disease-specific formulations, the Jan Aushadhi nutraceuticals Basket is making nutrition supplements more accessible to people across India. Nutrition for Diverse Needs The Jan Aushadhi portfolio is designed to respond to the varied needs of young, old, women, and people with different health issues. The range includes protein supplements, immunity products, nutritional foods and specialised formulations for individuals with specific dietary requirements. Manufactured in accordance with prescribed quality standards and offered at affordable prices, these products aim to make regular nutritional support more accessible without placing an undue burden on household budgets . Convenient Nutrition for Active Lifestyles Nutrient-dense Jan Aushadhi Protein Bar & Jan Aushadhi Immunity Bar offer a portable source of nourishment for children, working professionals and fitness enthusiasts. Available in chocolate flavour in a 35-gram pack, protein bar provides a convenient way to supplement daily protein intake while on the go. Enriched with Immunity-Supporting Ingredients tasty Immunity Bar provides energy and strengthens body’s protective barriers. These nutrition bars offer an economical alternative for consumers craving a quick snack but averse to junk food. For a more substantial protein supplement, 100% Whey Protein Powder & Jan Aushadhi Protein Powder support daily protein intake and muscle recovery, making it suitable for fitness enthusiasts. Protein Powder is available in Vanilla and Kesar Pista flavours, giving consumers greater choice. Supporting Women's Nutritional Needs Women have distinct nutritional requirements at different stages of life.  Jan Aushadhi Women Protein Boost is formulated to support daily protein intake, energy levels, and healthy bones and muscles. Available in chocolate and vanilla flavours, the 250-gram pack is priced at ₹204.66. By offering specialised nutrition at affordable rates, this product seeks to make it easier for more women to incorporate nutritional supplementation into their daily routines. Nutrition Designed for Specific Health Needs For individuals managing specific health conditions such as Diabetes, Kidney problems etc, dietary requirements can be more complex. Diabetes Care Protein Powder from JanAushadhi complements the nutritional requirements of people living with diabetes. For individuals with kidney-related conditions, Renal Care Protein Powder is available in both Low Protein and High Protein variants, allowing the choice of formulation to be guided by medical advice and individual dietary needs.
